newsitem.title: UK: DHL UK ups revenue 15m stg to 70m in Q1 96.
newsitem.headline: DHL UK ups revenue 15m stg to 70m in Q1 96.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said its UK operation had increased its revenue to 70 million stg in January-March this year from 55 million stg in the first quarter of 1996.

UK managing director Nick Butcher told a news briefing here that his division's aim, announced three years ago, to double its annual turnover from 150 million stg then to 300 million stg by 2000 could be achieved by the end of 1997.
"If that is achieved then it would be a fantastic achievement on behalf of our sales team," he said.
But he warned that the effects of the UK general election on May 1 could slow the 25 percent year-on-year turnover currently being experienced to around the 20-23 percent mark.
"After the election and whichever party wins, we expect interest rates to go up and it will be interesting to see what effect that has on the value of sterling," said Butcher.
He added that DHL had won a number of ex-UK express freight contracts from overseas, mainly hi-tech business company clients which had heavily invested in UK projects.
Many of these had established bases in Britain to act as footholds into the European Union, he told Reuters, and therefore were dependent on exports.

"The cloud on the horizon is the currency appreciation on UK exports. We have seen no sign of this having any (negative) effect on exports so far but there are worries about (this happening in) the future," he said.

"If sterling continues on its upward trend, then we may have to be satisfied with a few percentage points drop on our UK revenue growth of 25 percent, a performance which I think is staggering," he added.

DHL's UK commercial director Glyn Jones said that if the value of sterling continued to rise and affected UK exports, and DHL business, the company would consider reducing its prices, spending more on advertising and increasing its sales force.
